title: Colts-Chiefs preview with Jesse Newell; can Indy rebound in prime time?
text: The Athletic's James Boyd and Jesse Newell preview the Indianapolis Colts' showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night. The Colts got embarrassed in their season opener, whereas the Chiefs flexed their muscles in a dominant victory. Can Indy rebound in prime time? Newell suggests that the Chiefs' iffy passing game could give the Colts a chance. Hosted by Simplecast, an AdsWizz company. title: How the Broncos get back on track in week 2! What's the GAMEPLAN? | Orange & Blue Today
text: It’s the Friday Gameplan Edition of Orange & Blue Today, and as Sean Payton always says, the NFL is either a crisis or a carnival — and last week was definitely the crisis. After a rough 31–10 loss to the Chiefs, the Broncos return home to Empower Field at Mile High needing to reset fast before the Jacksonville Jaguars come to town. So how do the Broncos attack the Jaguars defense. Will they feature JK Dobbins more after he and RJ Harvey looked good on limited touches. Can Davis Webb get the run game going early, or does Sean Payton need to step in and steady the offense. On defense, tackling must improve immediately. The Broncos couldn’t slow down Kansas City’s rushing attack, and now they face a high‑powered Jaguars offense with multiple ways to stress a defense. How does Denver clean things up, and what’s their plan for stopping Trevor Lawrence — a quarterback who thrives in tight‑window throws — and a passing game featuring Parker Washington. The Broncos cannot afford to fall to 0–2, and this episode breaks down exactly what Denver must do to get back on the right track. 🔥 In this episode: How Denver flushes last week’s loss and resets for Week 2 What the Broncos’ offensive gameplan looks like vs Jacksonville Whether Dobbins and Harvey get more early involvement How Denver improves tackling and run defense How to defend Trevor Lawrence’s tight‑window passing attack Drop your take — what’s the biggest adjustment Denver must make to beat the Jaguars.

title: Jeff Legwold joins Kreckman and Lindahl 9-18-26
text: Let's take a look at this Broncos defense here for a moment. In fact, let's ask Jeff Legwald about it right now here on the Crankman and Lindahl Show as we are joined by Jeff Legwald of ESPN here on a Bud Light Football Friday. And Leggy, let's talk about the Denver defense first. Last year, Trevor Lawrence had a very good day. Parker Washington had a very good day against Denver. Defense didn't look great in week one either. What do you expect to see in terms of adjustments from Vance Joseph for this game? Well, I think, you know, Nate, I think you have to look at it sort of as they, from their lens, and their lens is, okay, the assignments were okay, but, you know, how they carried them. I've said this after the game and this week that, Schematically, not the issue. It was just getting it done. You know, tackling is not a strategic problem. You know, tackling is a football problem. And I think, you know, the Broncos are going to feel like that they'll have a good plan for Lawrence and the Jags, but they have to just get much better at the basic things, you know, And it sounds almost too simple, but it's true. Get off blocks, and when you're in position, get the ball carrier on the ground. So that's a different mindset than, hey, we've got to come up with this really creative plan to handle this offense. They feel like they have that, and they felt like they had it against the Chiefs. It's more a matter of, okay, you have to actually accomplish the the task at hand. The plan can be great, but if you don't tackle people and get off blocks and stay in the correct gap, it won't matter what the plan is. What do you think... Boy, Jeff, I don't even know how to really phrase the question. What do you expect out of Bo to start this game? Nate and I were just talking about it. Nate went back, looked at some numbers, looked at some video, not throwing a waddle as much. I know it was a heavy... course of the questioning today and Sean promising they're going to get Waddle the ball. Do you think we're going to see a force feed of the screen game or what do you think they're going to try to do to unlock the guy they gave up a first round pick for? Well, he's open on plenty of plays. I've been through the chart of the game twice and have been through it plenty and even watching it live. He's open including the first play of the game. That's a fact that If Bo simply gets the ball out of his hand, when Waddle flashes across the formation, it's a huge gain, and you may not even be having the narrative they had, you know, right now. So he is open. It's, you know, quarterback's got to put the ball in there, and Waddle's just got to continue to do what he does. And, you know, he's getting good releases. Now, he got bracketed a lot, so that is going to make Bo shy away in some initial progressions. But there were plays that were there when he was open. And when you get the chances and the opportunity when he isn't bracketed, that's when you've got to find a way to get him the ball. Because you can... You can force that to not happen from time to time. You can scheme it up so he doesn't get doubled. You can put him in a bunch. You can move him. And they did those things. And when he's in those situations, they've got to get him the ball. I don't think they can go into it thinking, okay, got to have 12 targets today or it's not a success. I think it's more a matter of every time you have done the right thing and gotten him free, that's when you've got to try to get him the ball in those situations. Jeff, there was a really high pressure rate on Bo Nix in that game. As you went and charted and looked it back, and I'll just tell you, as I rewatched the game, my conclusion was it was a bad footwork and a bad pocket presence game out of Bo Nix, which really he took himself out of the ability to be able to make the plays when they were there further down the field. What was your conclusion as to kind of where the poor place stemmed from? I think, you know, A, you know, I think in all of our jobs in the world, there are moments when you can be pushing too hard to succeed. The caged mountain lion thing? Yeah, no, I think sometimes he gets really, really intense sometimes. And that's one of his great qualities when you're in the two-minute drill or something or when it's tight or when bad things are happening. But I think over the course of his career, if he has a mistake early in the game, it sometimes takes him a minute to recover and sort of recalibrate himself. And that is a hard thing for a player. I'm not saying it's easy, but I've seen it over and over, especially an interception. If he has an interception early in the game, I think if you go back and look at his QBR and all of it in the four or five possessions after a pick, I think you're going to find that it's a tough bounce back. And now you got fooled a little bit Monday because they come right back. Touchdown drive, yeah. And he's five for five on the touchdown drive. But I think some of the damage quote unquote was, was done a little bit. Cause he, he never really got himself back in that rhythm and they didn't do him any favors, you know, give them some play action, uh, give them a few, uh, just run rundowns where he, he hands the ball off and completes the, you know, fake and watches the running back do his thing. Uh, You know, if your quarterback's having an unsettled night, I don't think keep dropping him back is the strategy you want to take. Because what happens there? They become the three-and-out offense when they're at their worst. And, you know, it all seems to fit together when they refuse to put the run game back in the equation. I would contend even... even a three and out or a one first down drive where you've run the ball four or five times is more helpful to settle your guy down than having him drop back and have to punt and do those things. And you guys know, I mean, you've heard me say it. I'm fascinated how NFL teams can live with 10 incompletions in a row and no one bats an eye. But if you have one run for two yards, the back doesn't see the ball again for 20 minutes. All right, talk about this Jacksonville team. What do they have to worry about with Jacksonville? What's the challenge that they're bringing in here? And how much of Travis Hunter offensively do you think we'll see? Well, they haven't used him much yet. I mean, it's still, you know, I think they're going to be very judicious. You know, and the trick to that is when you put a guy in, then, you know, everybody knows something's up. So, you know, it's harder, almost more difficult to use him in a spot duty on offense and get them free. But, you know, the athleticism is undeniable there. So I think they'll be, you know, I think they're going to perceive it as, you know, some coaches call it specials. You know, those plays are specials. They're going to be on the lookout for those if he appears on offense. And, you know, overall, it's a well put together team. You know, what have they won? eight, nine games in a row, regular season games in a row. I think they're averaging 31 points a game over that stretch. That's big time football. You know, that's getting it done on offense. Yeah, no doubt, and Trevor Lawrence absolutely has it going. He's Jeff Legwald, everybody. Read his stuff. ESPN.com, that's where you get Leggy's reporting on what's going on with the Broncos. Plus, Leggy's doing a lot of video work. I've been digging it. Good stuff in there, Jeff. We appreciate it, man. Thank you. No one wants to see that, really, but that's okay. Jeff, you're very good on camera. You have a likable face, and you present with an air of authority. When I watch Jeff Legwald, I'm like, I'm learning football. I trust that guy. Jeff, you present with an air of authority, but you have a punchable face. Yes, that's been said many times. I mean, that's the thing you can't do anything about. I've taken more than my share on the west side of Chicago. No, hey, listen. Yeah, and other things. You've got hobbies as well that seem to call that up, but okay. Jeff, man, we appreciate it as always. Thank you. Oh, thank you. Thank you very much. See you guys. Happy Friday. All right. Jeff Legwald with us on a Bud Light football Friday. Come see us here at Skippy's.
